title: Bengaluru's October Table: Bar Find Residency, a Bengali Feast and a New Lucknowi Room
excerpt: The Hindu's October guide maps a travelling Kolkata bar at Circa 11 until January 10, Taiyaba Ali's 14-seat Lucknowi dining room in Cox Town, and Amar Khamar's ingredient-first Bengali feast at The Oberoi.
body:
• Bar Find, the travelling bar that began in Kolkata, has taken a three-month residency at Circa 11 in Indiranagar, running October 9 to January 10, 2027.
  • At SEHN, a 14-seat dining room in Cox Town, chef Taiyaba Ali serves a home-style Lucknowi menu built around vegetable kawabs, chaats, pulaos and sheer khurma ice cream.
  • The month's guide also includes a Bengali feast at The Oberoi presented by Amar Khamar, the Kolkata enterprise known for folk rice varieties, and a bread-focused cafe, Toast House.
  • Reader check: SEHN seats 14 and opens for dinner Thursday to Saturday only - reservations are essential; Bar Find runs through January 10, so there is no October rush.

Bengaluru's October food calendar is unusually regional this year. The month's new openings and residencies, catalogued in The Hindu's October food guide, run from a Lucknowi home kitchen in Cox Town to a Kolkata travelling bar in Indiranagar and a Bengali feast at The Oberoi - a map of how India's city restaurants increasingly cook from specific homes and districts rather than generic regional menus.

A Lucknowi home, not a Lucknowi restaurant

At SEHN Dining Room on Wheeler Road in Cox Town, chef, writer and researcher Taiyaba Ali has built a 14-seat menu in three sections: experimental small plates, traditional large plates served like a daawat, and desserts rooted in Lucknow homes. The small plates include vegetable kawabs, hot and cold chaats, dal gosht dumplings and prawns with hari mirch hing achar. The large plates centre on pulaos and in-house breads, and desserts include sheer khurma ice cream, mukku baraf with fermented plum, cumin and black salt, and a Russel Market meetha paan.

"Leaving out the obvious dishes from the dining-room menu isn't a rejection of them. It's a way of making space for another story."

- Taiyaba Ali, chef, SEHN Dining Room

Ali deliberately leaves out the shaami and galouti kebabs most diners expect from Lucknow, drawing instead on the Muslim home she grew up in and the homes of friends. SEHN opens for dinner Thursday through Saturday, and at 14 seats it is a reservation-first room.

Bar Find settles into Circa 11

Bar Find, which began as a hidden bar in Kolkata and has since travelled to Mumbai, is resident at Circa 11 in Indiranagar from October 9 to January 10, 2027. The cocktail menu by co-founder and creative director Matteo Ciarpaglini includes the Spumante Marino, made with tomato water, marine cordial, olives and clarified bergamot; a Gilda Martini inspired by the Spanish pintxo; and a Ceviche Mary with vodka, leche de tigre and a flower-and-corn cordial. Sweeter serves include Pistachio & Coffee, an espresso-martini reinterpretation with cognac and vanilla-pistachio foam, and a Sgroppino of sparkling wine, lemon liqueur and ice cream.

Circa 11's own seasonal menu runs alongside, with grilled confit cabbage, lamb tostada, red snapper ceviche, biang biang noodles and seafood orzo among the plates, and desserts including a chocolate pave and the house tiramisu. The Nod Mag's October roundup also places Bar Find among the month's national highlights, noting Circa 11's stuffed chicken wings alongside the residency drinks.

A Bengali feast and the rest of the month

The guide's headline feast comes from Amar Khamar at The Oberoi. Amar Khamar - the name means "my farm" - is a Kolkata social enterprise founded in 2019 that works with farmers, mostly women, on folk rice varieties and hyperlocal Bengal produce such as lentils, honey, ghee, jaggery and spices, retailed through its Annaja store. Its Bengaluru appearance brings that ingredient-first Bengali cooking to a hotel table, a contrast with the restaurant Bengali canon of kosha mangsho and biryani that Amar Khamar pointedly avoids in its own Kolkata lunch room.

Also new this month: Toast House, the bread-focused cafe featured in the guide, and Roastery's latest outlet, Bengaluru House in Banashankari II Stage - about 4,000 square feet with seating for roughly 80, pouring coffee sourced almost entirely from Chikmagalur alongside a Hold-in-Hand sandwich range, pastas and flatbread pizzas. For Bengaluru's large Bengali, Awadhi and North Indian communities - and for visiting families from the diaspora - October offers three distinct regional tables within a few kilometres of each other.
